titleEn: When a Customer Comes, Say Hello!

pages.text: Jingle! At the doorbell, Coco, a little mouse in a red headscarf, hid behind the bread shelf. Mr. Pig, who carried flour sacks, came in. "I want to greet him like Mom..."
Bakery Mom, with flour on her arms, greeted him brightly. "Hello!" Coco tried too, but the hello stuck in their throat. Only their paws wriggled.
Mr. Pig set down the sack, then left with a jingle. Coco peeped over the shelf. Their mouth turned down. "I couldn't do it today either..."

Mom met Coco's eyes. "It doesn't have to be long. Just one hello is enough. When the door opens, alley light falls on the floor, right? Give that light a little bow." Coco stared at the floor by the door.
Mom opened the door a little. Alley light stretched across the floor. Coco bowed to the light and said softly, "Hello..." Mom sang, "When a customer comes, say hello!"
Jingle! Mr. Pig came back with another sack. Alley light spread over the floor. Coco took one step out from behind the shelf.
Coco tightened the scarf knot with both paws, then bowed to the light. "Hello!" Their paws trembled, but their voice didn't tremble at all.
Mr. Pig set down the sack and smiled wide. "Hello, Coco! What a big greeting today!" Coco's smile reached their ears. The shop seemed to grow brighter.
When the next customer came in, Coco stepped out in front of the shelf and bowed first. "One, light comes in, take a step! Two, bow! Three, hello!" The greeting no longer stuck in Coco's throat.

Mom lifted Coco and carried them to the doorway. "That was a wonderful greeting!" Even if you feel shy, one word can make a customer smile. Coco looked toward the door and called, "When a customer comes, say hello!"
